newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-FRAZIER IS UPSET IN OKLAHOMA.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-FRAZIER IS UPSET IN OKLAHOMA.

text.p: Sixth-seed Amy Frazier was upset as the $164,250 Oklahoma Classic tennis tournament on Monday.
Frazier, 30th in the Corel WTA Tour rankings, was stunned 7-6 (9-7) 7-5 by 19-year-old Italian Francesca Lubiana.
Lisa Raymond, the fourth seed, survived a 5-7 6-2 7-5 first-round match against Karin Kschwendt.
Most of the big-name players had the day off.
Lubiana, ranked 110th, needed a tiebreaker to best Frazier in the first set 7-6 (9-7).
The second set appeared headed for elimination with Frazier leading 40-love and trailing Lubiana just 6-5.
But Lubiana quickly tied the game at 40-all and closed out the match.
"When I was down 40-love," Lubiana said, "I played every point to win and tried to push the action."
Frazier had played well before in this tournament, winning the title in 1990 and reaching the semifinals in 1992, 1994 and 1995.
"She hit three clean winners when it was 40-love," Frazier said of the final set. "She's young and has a really good game. "She just played better today."
Raymond became ill with a possible case of the flu in her first-round match, and she fell behind 5-0 in the first set to Kschwendt.
Raymond, ranked 26th, fought back to tie the first set at 5-5 before losing 7-5. She then won the next two sets in the match which lasted one hour and 50 minutes.
